FR-I4: partly built: operational healing (rollback and probe incidents need no model and no person), engineering repair (a defect needs no decision, the gate merges a warranted repair by policy, a refused repair escalates to a person) and product adaptation (change requests and new requirements wait for a business or product owner) are built and tested by FR-I4-AC-1 to AC-3; factory learning's human promotion is built (FR-K3-AC-1, FR-K1-AC-3). not built: the paired evaluation the factory-learning loop should run before a person promotes a change (kernel/learn.py proposes a default check when a lesson recurs in two products, with no paired trial, effect size or interval); the pre-approved repair classes are fixed in code (a defect, a gate-warranted merge) rather than a list a person maintains; and the hand-off from operations to repair is not automated: an incident card's verdicts (rollback, open_defect) are recorded, but nothing in the kernel carries them out.
FR-I5: not built: no user metric is collected from a running release, so no release's impact on one is estimated, staggered or otherwise (the nearest thing is the canary of FR-H4, which compares the candidate's error rate with the current release's on the same replayed sample to promote or abort); incidents record what failed (probe results, canary numbers) and have no cause field, so no cause is marked a hypothesis either. It would take product metrics read from each release, a rollout staggered by environment or cohort, a comparison reported with an interval, and a cause field whose only allowed mark for a single incident is hypothesis.
FR-J1: partly built: the factory reverts a release that cannot start in production to the last green release, frees the lane of a dead holder, and tells a person when a revert fails (FR-J1-AC-1 to AC-3); it also retries apparatus failures (FR-J2-AC-1), resumes after a model outage (FR-J2-AC-2) and supersedes a waiting release when main moves (FR-Q5-AC-1). not built: a production process that crashes while serving is only reported (one incident per release, FR-I2), never restarted or reverted by the factory; there is no switch to a fallback model endpoint and no recall of a stalled cell; and the live view (kernel/status.py live) reads the lease file rather than the lock, so a dead holder's cell still shows as running until the lane is leased again.
FR-K1: partly built: a defect leaves a lesson and a regression criterion (FR-K2), lessons are grouped by class across products, a class recurring in two products becomes a proposal a person promotes into a default check that every new product's gate enforces (FR-K1-AC-1 to AC-3, FR-K3-AC-1), and builder reliability is measured from the ledgers (FR-F8). not built: incidents (failing probes, rollbacks) leave no lesson, because an incident card's open_defect verdict is not carried out; a closed defect leaves no sweep for its class and no eval case; there are no fire drills; and nothing measures whether a class of failure becomes rarer, so 'stronger' is not yet shown by a number.
FR-J4: not built: weekly fire drills that inject faults and score the factory on held-out scenarios. It would take a scheduler for drills, a fault catalogue (endpoint down, lane lock held, corrupt record, slow model) and a scorecard kept as evidence.
FR-K4: partly built: autonomy levels 1-4 capped per factory and per project, set by a person with a reason and enforced by the kernel (kernel/autonomy.py). Not built: a level per class of change (requirement change, model update, infrastructure change, dependency update), which needs a class on every change card and a policy table.
